name: MitID Ecosystem Reevaluation
consequences: Reevaluating the MitID ecosystem could lead to a deeper understanding of its complexities and dependencies, potentially revealing new avenues for reducing dependence on Apple and Google.
options: Develop a comprehensive mapping of the MitID dependency surface, including platform integrity assumptions, app-distribution constraints, and architectural conditions required for a platform-neutral or fallback trust model.
Conduct a thorough analysis of the ecosystem's conservative and certification-heavy nature, identifying potential entry points for influencing AltID and related procurement decisions.
Explore alternative authentication protocols and standards that could be integrated into MitID, reducing its reliance on Apple and Google.
review: This reevaluation might uncover hidden dependencies or vulnerabilities in the current system, but it may also delay progress toward a platform-neutral solution.

name: AltID Involvement
consequences: Influencing AltID could lead to the inclusion of platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements in official design, policy, consultation, or procurement documents.
options: Engage with AltID stakeholders to incorporate requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms into its design and development process.
Collaborate with AltID developers to integrate open standards such as FIDO2/WebAuthn and OpenID Connect on GrapheneOS or comparable Android-compatible platforms.
Advocate for the inclusion of a browser-based or hardware-token-based fallback authentication path in AltID, reducing dependence on the mobile OS duopoly.
review: Securing AltID's commitment to platform-neutrality and fallback access might be challenging due to existing dependencies and technical complexities.

name: EU Engagement
consequences: Engaging with EU bodies and technical working groups could lead to the alignment of Danish advocacy with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in.
options: Participate in EU-level discussions and working groups related to the European Digital Identity Wallet framework, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms.
Collaborate with EU stakeholders to develop common standards and requirements for digital identity systems, promoting supplier-neutrality and fallback-capability design.

Engage with relevant EU bodies to ensure that Danish procurement processes and AltID development reflect European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in.
review: EU-level engagement might be challenging due to existing bureaucratic complexities and competing interests among member states.

name: Procurement Pressure
consequences: Applying procurement pressure could lead to the inclusion of platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements in official AltID-related design, policy, consultation, or procurement documents.
options: Engage with relevant procurement bodies to ensure that AltID development reflects European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in.
Advocate for the inclusion of platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in official procurement documentation and tender processes.
Collaborate with procurement stakeholders to develop common standards and requirements for digital identity systems, promoting supplier-neutrality and fallback-capability design.
review: Applying procurement pressure might be challenging due to existing dependencies and technical complexities within the AltID ecosystem.

name: Demonstrator Development

options: Develop a mobile-oriented demonstrator authenticating against a simulated Danish public-sector identity-provider environment using open standards such as FIDO2/WebAuthn and OpenID Connect on GrapheneOS or comparable Android-compatible platforms.
Explore a browser-based or hardware-token-based fallback authentication path in a secondary demonstrator, reducing dependence on the mobile OS duopoly altogether.
Collaborate with developers to integrate open standards into AltID's design and development process, ensuring platform-neutrality and fallback access.
review: Developing credible demonstrators might be challenging due to existing technical complexities within the MitID ecosystem.
